title: AzureGate Implementation: Ops intake and network handshake
next_steps: Redwood to send VPC peering checklist and example CloudFormation by 2027-12-01
Customer to share CIDR ranges and peering window by 2027-12-03
Schedule dedicated network runbook call with networking team week of 2027-12-06
Redwood SE to provision staging tenant and run perf bench by 2027-12-06
action_items: Priya Menon: Provide CIDR ranges + current NAT/gateway topology by 2027-12-03
Evelyn Cho (Redwood SE): Setup staging tenant, enable KV cache logs, run 2 workload benchmarks by 2027-12-06
Marco Ruiz: Share onboarding runbook, pricing contact, and trial Reserved-Capacity options by 2027-12-01
Connor Zhang: Confirm egress firewall rules and list of IPs to whitelist by 2027-12-02
meeting_header:
Date: 2027-11-28
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Evelyn Cho (Redwood SE), Noah Grant (Redwood Support), Liam O'Connor (AzureGate VP Eng), Priya Menon (SRE Lead), Connor Zhang (DevOps), Sara Lieu (Security), Maya Rishi (PM)
summary: Kickoff focused on network/VPC peering requirements, security controls (SAML/SCIM, KMS), staging benchmark plan, and timeline for pilot. Customer emphasized strict egress policies and SOC2 audit in Q1. Agreed next steps: share VPC checklist, customer to provide CIDR ranges, Redwood to spin staging tenant and run benchmarks, follow-up network deep-dive next week.
transcript:
[00:00] Jasmine Patel: Hi everyone thanks for joining, we can do quick intros and then jump into the ops and network items, we have about 45 minutes so we should be able to cover the checklist and next steps.
[00:10] Liam O'Connor: Yep, hi all, Liam here, thanks for coordinating. We want to get this on the fast track, Q1 audit looms so network and data residency are the blockers.
[00:22] Marco Ruiz: Marco from Redwood, I'll own the onboarding cadence and make sure the CSM side is set.
[00:30] Priya Menon: Priya, SRE, we're most concerned about peering rules, NAT/transit gateways, and egress policies. Also curious about the dedicated option cause we may need isolated capacity.
[00:45] Evelyn Cho: Evelyn, Redwood SE — I'll be the technical lead on the migration and the perf bench. Quick note: we support Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) deployments; sometimes my notes come out as Redwoode Dedicated in the transcript so ignore typos.
[01:05] Connor Zhang: Connor, DevOps — we'll need IPs to whitelist and the exact CIDR ranges, please.
[01:12] Sara Lieu: Hi, Sara from security — SOC2 and encryption at rest are mandatory for us, KMS integration is high priority.
[01:20] Jasmine Patel: Great, let's jump into network. Evelyn can you run us through the VPC peering flow and what we need from AzureGate?
[01:29] Evelyn Cho: Sure. For our Private deployment we do a VPC peering (or VNet peering in Azure terms), we need your CIDR blocks, subnets for peering, and any transit gateway/NVA details. We'll share a peering template and CF script — some customers use Terraform, others CloudFormation — in Azure we'll provide an ARM example.
[01:50] Priya Menon: Two quick things: we use /16 for the production VNet and /20 for staging, we use forced-tunnel egress through our transit NGW, and we do no-ip-public outbound unless through proxy. Will that be a problem?
[02:05] Evelyn Cho: Not a blocker. We'll ask for the exact NAT IPs you want us to use, and we can route egress through a peered path. For forced-tunnel there are caveats, we might need a small egress NAT for health checks and image pulls; we'll document options.
[02:22] Noah Grant: Also want to flag rate limits and burst behavior — in Dedicated we can bump concurrency to keep latency, but hosted has per-tenant throttles.
[02:35] Maya Rishi: From product: our success criteria are sub-200ms median token latency for the customer-facing feature and consistent cost per 10k tokens under their budget threshold.
[02:48] Evelyn Cho: Ok noted. For latency targets we will run a tail-latency bench in staging with your typical prompt distribution; I'll need a sample prompt set.
[03:02] Priya Menon: We'll provide a representative set by Friday.
[03:08] Jasmine Patel: Next security piece, Sara — do you have requirements for SSO/SAML and SCIM and audit logs?
[03:15] Sara Lieu: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning is mandatory. We also require audit logs retention for 12 months with immutable storage if possible. Does Redwood support KMS integration with customer-managed keys?
[03:30] Evelyn Cho: Yes — customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption but not always CMK in early previews, I'll confirm the exact availability (sometimes mis-labeled in docs as KMS/HSM beta). We'll share the security pack.
[03:49] Liam O'Connor: For compliance we need to know the certification matrix — any SOC2 or ISO certs?
[03:56] Marco Ruiz: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have ISO 27001 in progress — we'll attach certification docs after the call.
[04:10] Priya Menon: Good. Next—observability and cost breakdowns. We want token-level cost breakdowns and tracing by route.
[04:20] Evelyn Cho: That's baked into Redwood Console — per-route token counts, model latency histograms, and trace hooks. We can enable high retention for a fee; we'll scope it.
[04:32] Connor Zhang: On networking do you require any peering keys or shared secrets?
[04:36] Evelyn Cho: No shared secrets for peering, mostly IP/CIDR and routing. For private links we might use private endpoints depending on region.
[04:45] Maya Rishi: Question on model variants — can we pin versions per route? We may want a canary.
[04:52] Evelyn Cho: Yes, you can pin versions and do canary rollouts with automatic fallback; we'll demo the rollout in a follow-up.
[05:00] Liam O'Connor: Let's talk capacity. We want predictable throughput during demo day in Jan — what's the reservation model?
[05:09] Marco Ruiz: Dedicated is reserved capacity — monthly or annual commits; we can do a short pilot with burst capacity enabled. Pricing contact will follow.
[05:20] Priya Menon: Any minimum commit?
[05:23] Marco Ruiz: We typically have a small monthly minimum for Dedicated pilots, but we'll share exact numbers. We can also start on hosted and move to Dedicated before the event if needed.
[05:35] Connor Zhang: Perf bench — what's the timeline?
[05:38] Evelyn Cho: We can spin staging in 48-72 hours once we have CIDR ranges and access, then run bench against a pinned model. Bench will measure p50/p95 latency and token cost.
[05:50] Priya Menon: Will you run with quantized models? We prefer 8-bit quantization for cost savings but worry about quality regressions.
[05:58] Evelyn Cho: We support quantized variants; Redwood Optimize suggestions will show quality tradeoffs. For initial bench we'll run both FP16 and INT8 variants if your workload allows.
[06:16] Liam O'Connor: On data handling — do logs include user-provided content? We need clarity for GDPR.
[06:24] Noah Grant: By default we retain logs for debugging but customer can opt out; for Private we don't persist user content to Redwood and you can control retention via the Console. We'll provide the retention matrix.
[06:38] Sara Lieu: Ok please also include retention in the security pack.
[06:44] Jasmine Patel: Quick note on SSO — we support SAML and OIDC; we also have SCIM for provisioning. Marco will share the SSO setup guide.
[06:55] Marco Ruiz: I'll drop the SSO/SCIM doc and a checklist after the call.
[07:03] Maya Rishi: Regarding the bench inputs — can you accept a zipped set of prompts and a small user-sim harness?
[07:09] Evelyn Cho: Yes, please supply prompts, expected outputs, and concurrency profile. We'll also instrument KV cache usage if you use persistent contexts.
[07:20] Priya Menon: We do a lot of system-context style chats that use the KV cache; how does Redwood handle KV cache eviction and cold starts?
[07:30] Evelyn Cho: We manage KV cache for LLM sessions and provide TTLs and explicit pinning; cold start can add latency but the cache warms quickly with prefix caching. Sometimes docs call it KV-ketch in auto transcripts, sorry about spelling.
[07:46] Connor Zhang: One more nit: egress logging — we have strict egress DLP, will Redwood provide request logs with destination?
[07:56] Noah Grant: Yes we can emit request logs with minimal PII and destination info; for more detailed egress info we recommend the private setup connected to your SIEM.
[08:10] Liam O'Connor: Can you run a quick sketch of the onboarding timeline?
[08:14] Jasmine Patel: Sure — Day 0: share docs and CIDRs; +72 hours: staging up; week 1: perf bench and SSO setup; week 2: pilot with limited traffic and monitoring; week 3: go/no-go for broader rollout/cliff. We'll adjust to your dates but that's the baseline.
[08:32] Priya Menon: Our audit freeze is early Feb, so we want pilot completed by end of Jan.
[08:37] Marco Ruiz: That maps fine — we'll prioritize your slot.
[08:42] Maya Rishi: What about model governance / evals? We need to capture quality regressions between model updates.
[08:48] Evelyn Cho: Redwood Optimize includes eval suites and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll onboard your evals and run nightly checks during pilot.
[08:58] Liam O'Connor: Any required firewall changes on our side?
[09:02] Evelyn Cho: Mainly whitelist Redwood egress IPs and allow peering. We'll provide the list and a small set of endpoints for health checks.
[09:12] Priya Menon: Ok — will do.
[09:15] Jasmine Patel: Let's capture the immediate next steps — Marco you'll send security pack and SSO guide; Evelyn you'll provision staging; Priya will send CIDRs.
[09:25] Marco Ruiz: Correct, I'll send an email with attachments by tomorrow EOD.
[09:29] Priya Menon: We'll try to get CIDRs by Friday.
[09:33] Maya Rishi: Quick Q: do you support regional model placement for EU data residency?
[09:39] Evelyn Cho: Yes — regional placement is supported in Private and Dedicated across supported cloud regions; Hosted is multi-region but we can opt customers into specific regions for residency.
[09:50] Liam O'Connor: A few other questions popped up in chat about throttles and quotas.
[09:55] Noah Grant: We'll include default quotas and quota bump process in the doc.
[10:00] Priya Menon: One security nuance: we use a third-party key management provider — can you integrate with external HSM?
[10:08] Evelyn Cho: We integrate with customer KMS providers supported by Azure; HSM-level integrations depend on the provider — we'll validate and include in the security pack.
[10:22] Jasmine Patel: We're about 10 minutes left, any last items?
[10:27] Connor Zhang: How do you handle model updates during pilot? We don't want surprises.
[10:31] Evelyn Cho: We keep model variants pinned and have rollout controls with automatic fallbacks; we'll only upgrade after sign-off.
[10:38] Priya Menon: For the bench, please include cost projection per 10k tokens at different batch sizes.
[10:45] Evelyn Cho: Will do; Redwood Optimize will recommend batching & quantization to hit cost targets.
[10:52] Maya Rishi: Can you also share a short troubleshooting runbook for common networking failures?
[10:58] Marco Ruiz: Yes, I'll attach a runbook.
[11:04] Liam O'Connor: Great, thanks all.
[11:06] Jasmine Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll recap and send notes. Next meeting: network deep-dive scheduled for 2027-12-06 — we'll share invite.
[11:15] Priya Menon: Thanks.
[11:20] (call ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions present (e.g., "Redwoode"), speaker labels sometimes condensed; natural speech: pauses, filler words, overlap. The call lasted ~48 minutes and covered onboarding, security, peering, staging and bench plans.
